tips.title: Ramadan tips
tips.disclaimer: General guidance, not medical or religious rulings. Ask your doctor about medicines and health conditions.

hydration.title: Spread water through the night
hydration.body: Drink a glass or two at iftar, more through the evening and some at suhoor, rather than all at once.

suhoor.title: Make suhoor slow and filling
suhoor.body: Whole grains, eggs or yoghurt, and fruit keep energy steadier than sugary or very salty foods.

iftar.title: Start iftar gently
iftar.body: Begin with something light and water, then eat the main meal after a short pause.

children.title: Children join the family meals
children.body: Young children eat normally through the day and share suhoor and iftar. Older children can try short practice fasts.

pregnancy.title: Pregnant or breastfeeding
pregnancy.body: Decide with your clinician and scholar. Either choice is fine, and Thuluth plans for both.

sleep.title: Protect sleep
sleep.body: A short rest in the afternoon helps when nights are short.

activity.title: Keep activity light
activity.body: Gentle walks are better than hard exercise during the fast; save harder exercise for after iftar.

medicines.title: Check medicines early
medicines.body: If anyone takes regular medicines, especially for diabetes, talk to the doctor before Ramadan.
